rule: Less predictable irregular past tenses — patterns in the group
objective: To spell irregular past-tense verbs by recognising vowel-pattern groups
defs: was aware of or had information about; past of know
became bigger or developed; past of grow
moved through the air; past of fly
selected or decided on; past of choose
became solid with cold; past of freeze
controlled and steered a vehicle; past of drive
used words to communicate; past of speak
split, cracked or smashed; past of break
had clothing or accessories on the body; past of wear

sentences.knew: She ____________________ the answer before the teacher had even finished asking the question.
sentences.grew: The tomato plants ____________________ so tall that summer that they reached the top of the greenhouse.
sentences.flew: The heron ____________________ low over the river, trailing its long legs just above the surface of the water.
sentences.chose: After reading all four books in the series, she ____________________ the third one as her clear favourite.
sentences.froze: The pond ____________________ solid overnight and by morning the ducks were sliding about on the ice.
sentences.drove: He ____________________ across the entire country in three days, stopping only to sleep and refuel.
sentences.woke: She ____________________ to the smell of toast and found her brother had already made breakfast for everyone.
sentences.spoke: The explorer ____________________ to the school about the six months she had spent in the Amazon rainforest.
sentences.broke: The world record ____________________ for the third time that year when the sprinter crossed the finish line.
sentences.wore: The knight ____________________ armour so heavy that two squires were needed to help him mount his horse.

starter.question: Can you write the past tense of each verb? What pattern do you spot?
starter.ruleBox: These verbs are irregular, but patterns emerge when grouped: know/knew, grow/grew, fly/flew all use -ew. Choose/chose, freeze/froze, drive/drove, wake/woke, speak/spoke, break/broke all use a long -o- sound. Wear/wore uses -ore. Group them and the pattern does half the work.

thisWeeksWordsQ: What do you notice about today's words?
thisWeeksWordsPrompt: Group today's words by their vowel sound. What do you spot?
thisWeeksWordsExplanation: All today's words are irregular past tenses, but they fall into patterns. Knew, grew and flew all end in -ew (from know, grow, fly). Chose, froze, drove, woke, spoke and broke all have a long -o- sound. Wore has the -ore pattern. Grouping irregular verbs by vowel pattern makes them far easier to learn and remember.

clicks.label: Base word
clicks.body: ceosan — to choose; the past form was ceas

clicks.label: Original meaning
clicks.body: ceosan meant to test, taste or pick out — related to German kiesen and Dutch kiezen.

clicks.label: Then
clicks.body: Old English ceosan became Middle English chosen/chesen. The past tense ceas became chose by the 1300s.

clicks.label: Now
clicks.body: We use chose as the simple past of choose: 'she chose the red one.'

clicks.label: In today's words
clicks.body: Chose, froze, drove, woke, spoke and broke all share the long -o- pattern in the past tense — even though their base verbs sound different.

wordSortQ: Can you sort these words into two groups?

wordSort.box2sub: Vowel changes to a long -o- sound
wordSort.hint: Look at the vowel in each past form. Does it end in -ew, or is there a long -o- sound?
wordSort.answerNote: -ew pattern: knew (know), grew (grow), flew (fly). Long -o- pattern: chose, froze, drove, woke, spoke, broke, wore.
wordSort.exampleLine: know → knew (-ew pattern) | choose → chose (long -o- pattern)

wordShed.sentence: He knew exactly where the treasure was buried, but he was not about to tell anyone else.

wordShed.morphology: know (v) → knew (past) → known (past part) → knowing (pres part) → knowledge (n) → unknown (adj) → knowledgeable (adj)
